ORDER [C272], at the generic FIXED ADD arm: a parenthesized RIGHT-hand ADD is evaluated FIRST and its sum parked (`a + (b + c)' -> LHLD b / PUSH H / LHLD c / POP D / DAD D / PUSH H / LHLD a / POP D / DAD D, E45S6); a parenthesized right-hand MUL stays LEFT-first (MB34 `n + (n*3)', MB35 `(n+1) + (n*3)', both reaching this arm and both byte-exact).  A parenthesized DIV, SUB, EXP or literal right operand is NOT measured at this arm -- R722 `a + (b/d)' goes through a decimal arm and LR19 `x + (-32768)' through the out-of-range-literal arm, so neither is evidence about this dispatch [E2E-40/P10a, spec/lab-evidence/e2e40-p10a/ARM-REACH.txt].

column4: DR's OPEN pushes one title-length byte and six option words, then passes the file's control-block address in HL to ?OIOOP. Titleless: 21 bytes, option word 0690H = 0x0400 declared-file + 0x0200 stream organisation + 0x0010 stream + 0x0080 input, words 2..6 built from the zero in B (MOV H,B / MOV L,B). With a literal-string TITLE: 29 bytes -- XRA A becomes LXI H,<pool bytes>; MVI A,<byte length>; CALL ?SLCTS (net +7), 0690H becomes 0E90H (the TITLE bit 0x0800) and w2 becomes LXI H,0000H because B now holds the title length (net +1). `input' and `stream' set the same bits, so either spelling lowers identically. An OPEN naming NO mode DEFAULTS TO INPUT and measures the same 0x0690: E46E4 `open file(f);' and E46G3 `open file(f) stream;' are both 0x0690 and E46G1 `open file(f) title(...)';' is 0x0E90, so the title bit composes with the default exactly as with a spelled mode [C286]. DR diagnoses a REPEATED option keyword, or two members of the exclusive mode group, as pass-2 CONFLICT and emits no .REL [C285].

CREATE:22 is not itself a specimen: CREATE refuses later, at its six-item PUT LIST on line 39, so the witness is E46F1 and the statement is only that DR's word for that shape is composed correctly here. column3: put file(f) list(<one or more literals>);
column4: A named-file PUT attaches with DE = 0x0652 and CALL ?SIOOP after LXI H over the file's control block, and the ITEM chain is the console chain UNCHANGED.  The attach word and the two literal classes are what this row's four objects measure: E16D/E17D for `list(<character literal>)' and `list(<integer literal>)', E46L5 and E46L16 for the same literal chain living alongside a VARIABLE item in one DATA image.  The measured relation between the two mode words is one bit: 0x0252 + 0x0400 (declared file) = 0x0652, as 0x0290 + 0x0400 = 0x0690 for the GET.  0x0652 is NOT 0x0400|0x0200|0x0010|0x0040 (that is 0x0650): the attach also carries 0x0002, whose PRINT reading in P0 section 3 belongs to OPEN words, and which no GET attach has (the 3 record-WRITE attaches read 0x0650 = 0x0652 minus exactly that bit) -- so within ATTACH words 0x0002 separates put list from write and from get; what is measured is that pairing, not the bit's meaning, which is why this is one lowering with a parameter and not a second copy of PUT.  A numeric literal does NOT go the fixed-variable route: `list(42)' is ?DLDOP at the digit count, ?QDCOP at digits+3 with scale 0, then ?PNVOP, and its packed cell is allocated through the same image-dedup table as every other DEC pool cell [C280].  The FOUR VARIABLE CLASSES are the next row's, and [C293] is the claim that the two rows share one generator.
column13: [E2E-42/P2a] the VARIABLE item is IMPLEMENTED and no longer belongs in this row's boundary -- see FILE.PUT_LIST_VAR, which carries the four authorized classes.  What still refuses here -- and the multi-item list this row used to refuse is LOWERED now [C296], so the literal chain simply runs N times: a SKIP/PAGE control item on a file (E41X6 in a list, E41X9 bare -- CREATE 01B3/01CA/01E9 run `?SKPOP' after a 0x0652 attach, and the bare form used to be lowered on the CONSOLE route silently [C300]), a file PUT EDIT (E41X8 -- P086K 001F `?EDITF ?DLDOP'), and any PUT on a stream whose OPEN this compiler refuses (PRINT, keyed, ENVIRONMENT, LINESIZE -- E41X5's family).  DR attaches 0x0652 even with NO open (P086K, and E46L8 reproduces that shape), so a refusal there is about no object of ours measuring the statement behind such an attach, not about DR forbidding it.  NO corpus program puts a LITERAL on a named file: the whole 44-program census holds exactly three `put file' statements (CREATE:39 six variables, KEYFILE:25 two, LOAN2 `list(clear)' a BIT(1)) -- and ALL THREE now get past this row, because the lists are multi-item [C296] and the classes are authorized: CREATE's line-39 six-item list and KEYFILE's line-25 two-item list LOWER here, and LOAN2 refuses at its line-39 STATIC declaration ([C114]) before any PUT is reached.  So this row refuses NO corpus `put file' statement at all and its corpus column is NONE -- a fact about the corpus, not about the feature; what CREATE and KEYFILE still fail on is elsewhere (CREATE: the SKIP control item at line 41, negative rows E41X6/E41X9; KEYFILE: the KEYED OPEN at line 16, FILE.OPEN_STREAM), and the literal route is carried entirely by E16D/E17D and by the two probes that mix a literal item with a variable one. column4: The named-file route takes the SAME item chain the console route takes for the same variable, byte for byte including the resolved operand address, and differs only in the stream-selection prologue (`LXI H,<fcb> / LXI D,0652 / LXI B,<stmt> / CALL ?SIOOP' against `LXI D,0252 / LXI B,<stmt> / CALL ?SYSPR'), both ending in `CALL ?QIOOP'.  Four classes are authorized, each by its own whole byte-exact object: CHARACTER VARYING `LXI H,*D,<v> / ?SLVTS / ?PNCOP' (E46L1 -- the cell ADDRESS, not the 2-word `LHLD' descriptor form ?Vrop uses on the GET side, which is what my own P1e design note wrongly predicted); CHARACTER FIXED `LXI H,*D,<v> / MVI A,<declared length> / ?SLCTS / ?PNCOP' (E46L2, width inline from the declaration, not from the cell); FIXED BINARY `LHLD <k> / MVI A,09 / ?QICOP / ?PNVOP' (E46L3, 2-word VALUE operand); FIXED DECIMAL `LXI H,*D,<z> / MVI A,p / ?DLDOP / MVI A,p+3 / MVI B,s / ?QDCOP / ?PNVOP' (E46L4, p+3 = 9 with p = 6, s = 0 AND s = 3 in one object).  The operand form is chosen by STORAGE CLASS and not by route -- [C291]'s console rule, generalised.  Authorization is a SEPARATE decision from lowering: `authorize_file_item' runs before the open guard and before a byte is emitted, so a refusal names the operand it refused.  The attach word comes from a lowered OUTPUT open and nothing else, keyed on the FILE operand rather than on the title's spelling, so a VARIABLE title composes with this route unchanged (E46L6 [C294]).  At runtime the FILE route's content is NOT the console's: DR's runtime apostrophe-QUOTES every character item on a stream file and NOT on the console, separates items with ONE BLANK, never line-terminates, pads an under-filled CHARACTER FIXED with BLANKS to the declared length, honours a varying item's length byte without padding, and prints FIXED BINARY in DECIMAL -- all measured on DR's own written files, and none of it emitted by this compiler [C295].
column13: Everything whose FILE-route bytes no object of ours measures, refused by name in `authorize_file_item' or in the matcher, each with the DR object that measures the verdict: an EXPRESSION (E46L9/E46M23 -- DR evaluates `k + 1' as `LHLD / INX H' and prints it), an ARRAY ELEMENT (E46L10/E46M22 -- DR folds a LITERAL subscript into the address), a FLOAT (E46L11/E46M21/E46M26), a POINTER and a whole structure, both of which DR REFUSES with `COMP REQ ?' and no object (E46M25, E46M24 -- [C290]'s absence is a measured refusal now [C301]), a BASED operand, a BIT(1), and a procedure FORMAL.  The internal CHARACTER member this row refused (E46L7) is LOWERED and byte-exact: DR's answer to the cold question is that a FIXED member carries its declared length (`MVI A,08 / ?SLCTS', E46M17) and members of both spellings share one cell (E46M18) [C297]; the authorization lives in FILE.PUT_LIST_MULTI / AGG.MEMBER_FILE_PUT now, and this row keeps the four SCALAR classes it measured.  Plus `put file(f)' on a file this compiler never opened for OUTPUT -- E46L8, PU1's own program, which DR compiles with a bare 0x0652 attach and no open at all.  `list(a, b)' is LOWERED [C296] -- E46M7, E46M8, E46M9, E46M10, E46M11, E46M14, E46M15 and E46M19 are byte-exact multi-item objects of this row's classes and E46M2 is the same two items as two statements; E46L5/E46L16 remain the sequential single-item specimens.   The three corpus `put file' statements are corroborating HISTORY, not this row's refusals, and the census -- not this prose -- is what names each program's ACTUAL current blocker (verified against the binary at this commit, `corpus_census.py`): CREATE:39's six-item `list(name,addr,city,state,zip,phone)' and KEYFILE:25's `list(name,k)' are MULTI-item lists that PARSE, BIND and LOWER -- the old "multi-item, so they stop before authorization is even reached" boundary was retired by [C296] and is NOT the reason either program refuses today.  CREATE's measured first blocker is the CONTROL item at line 41, `PUT FILE(OUTPUT) LIST item 1 is the control item SKIP, unmeasured on the named-file route' (negative rows E41X6/E41X9), and KEYFILE's is three statements EARLIER, the OPEN at line 16, `OPEN option KEYED is outside what this compiler lowers', so its line-25 PUT is never reached -- and CREATE:22's variable TITLE has been lowered since [C288].  LOAN2 refuses at its line-39 declaration (`STATIC on CHAR(14) VARYING is unsampled', [C114]), long before any PUT, so its `list(clear)' BIT(1) behind a PRINT open is a SECOND, separate unsupported construct that this compiler currently never gets to see.  What this row therefore licenses is nothing about CREATE's or KEYFILE's COMPLETE program: multi-item COMPOSITION is SUPPORTED and byte-exact on measured probes, the authorized member and scalar classes are SUPPORTED within the perimeter above, and the corpus programs are corroboration of the STRUCTURE only.

column4: ONE `?SIOOP' and ONE `?QIOOP' per STATEMENT, whatever N is, with the N item chains concatenated in SOURCE ORDER and NOTHING emitted between one item and the next; an item that appears twice is emitted twice.  The law is arithmetic, not stylistic: E46M1's two-item file PUT spans 37 bytes (12 + 11 + 11 + 3, addresses 0023-0048) where E46M2's two one-item PUTS of the same two items span 26 + 26 = 52 (0023-003C and 003D-0057), and the STATEMENT-LEVEL saving is 52 - 37 = 15 bytes = one attach (12) plus one close (3) the multi-item form does not duplicate.  Do NOT quote the whole-program CODE difference, 115 - 96 = 19, as that saving: it is a different measurement of two programs that differ by more than one attach, because E46M1 also carries a 34-byte CONSOLE put list('A','B') that E46M2 has no counterpart of -- 44 fixed bytes + 37 + 34 = 115 against 44 + 26 + 26 = 96, so 19 = 34 - 15 [C296]. CREATE's six-item list spelled with ordinary variables is byte-exact as one object (E46M19), which is the corpus shape (CREATE, KEYFILE) reproduced as a probe -- corpus programs cannot be witnesses [tools/coverage_check.py], so the probes carry the claim and the corpus carries the corroboration. The lowering change that made this true was in the MATCHER alone: `lower_put_items_gen' has folded over an item list since [E2E-29/P1] [C293][C296].

column4: RESOLUTION IS NOT AUTHORIZATION. Making the member's NAME resolve must not silently enable the operations a CHARACTER variable has, because DR has no object for any of them on an internal member. The compiler therefore gives the member its own kind (codegen's Vimem) rather than reusing Vvar/Vfix, so a route admits it only by naming that kind; the eleven routes here do not, and each refuses with a [TBD] that NAMES the member and its storage class. Three of the fifteen (K10, K11, K15) stop on a guard that predates this milestone and fires for ordinary variables too -- pinned because they show the name resolution did not open them; K12 is bind's ambiguity stop, required by correctness independently of DR because two rows share one key and the first would win silently.
